name: manifold
why: A robust geometry kernel for manifold meshes, close to the mathematics of solids and worth a deeper look.

brief.what_it_is: Manifold is a C++ geometry library for creating and operating on manifold triangle meshes, meaning meshes that represent closed solid objects. It takes in manifold meshes, which it can build with OpenSCAD-style constructors or from signed-distance functions via a level-set function, or external mesh data, which it rejects with an error status if the mesh is not manifold. It outputs manifold meshes from Boolean operations (union, difference and similar), smoothing and refinement, and file I/O. It has bindings for C, JS/TS via WASM, Python, and several other languages.
brief.why_it_exists: The author says the primary goal is reliability: "guaranteed manifold output without caveats or edge cases." The secondary goal is performance through parallelization. The README calls a robust mesh Boolean algorithm "an open problem for many years" and claims the guaranteed-manifold Boolean is possibly the first of its kind.
brief.how_it_works: The core is a guaranteed-manifold mesh Boolean algorithm, which the README describes as the library's most significant contribution and as the basis for a CAD kernel. It uses vertex properties and IDs to track materials and which input object or face each surface came from. Parallelism comes through TBB when enabled, with a serial fallback for small problems and a serial-only WASM build. The README gives no deeper algorithm detail beyond links to the wiki.

brief.install_notes: Only CMake, a C++ compiler, and Python are needed to build the core (tested with GCC, LLVM and MSVC). Optional dependencies add features: TBB for parallelism (strongly encouraged), Nanobind for Python bindings, Emscripten for JS/WASM, GTest for tests, Assimp for extras utilities, and Tracy for profiling. Missing dependencies are downloaded by default (MANIFOLD_DOWNLOADS=ON), and offline builds can point FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_* at local sources. Package managers: vcpkg for C++, npm (manifold-3d), PyPI (manifold3d), Maven, NuGet, crates.io and others. Windows users are advised to build with -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF. The WASM build needs Node.js plus Emscripten, installed via brew on macOS or emsdk on Linux. The CI workflow manifold.yml is the reference for platform-specific steps.
brief.standout: Few mesh-Boolean tools promise guaranteed manifold output, and the README says it is probably the first to do so. The project also refuses to write STL files as a matter of design and points users to 3MF or glTF with the EXT_mesh_manifold extension instead. It has an unusually long user list (OpenSCAD, Blender, Godot, BRL-CAD and others), and the author says the OpenSCAD-style samples are a deliberate nod to his own OpenSCAD designs.
brief.status: Probably maintained, but the README gives no release or commit date and I did not check the repository's release page. Evidence of ongoing work: it includes recent features such as MANIFOLD_NO_IOSTREAM, the npm and PyPI packages are linked with version badges, a Rust port was added, and the CI setup is referenced. Treat the activity level as unverified.
brief.caveats: Inputs that are not manifold produce an error, and the README says the Merge function only fixes slightly non-manifold meshes, so some files will need external repair tools. STL export is discouraged because it loses topology. OBJ I/O is limited and mainly for testing. The WASM build is serial-only, and MANIFOLD_PAR with Emscripten is not recommended because of possible memory corruption. The built-in TBB option causes duplicate TBB copies if other libraries bundle their own, and the README warns against installing that build. MANIFOLD_ASSERT adds about 20% runtime overhead. Polygon triangulation is serial. The README does not state a license, so I could not check it.
quotes: Our primary goal is reliability: guaranteed manifold output without caveats or edge cases.
This library is fast with guaranteed manifold output.
Please avoid saving to STL files! They are lossy and inefficient - when saving a manifold mesh to STL there is no guarantee that the re-imported mesh will still be manifold, as the topology is lost.

judge.reason: Its mesh-Boolean kernel tackles a long-standing geometric robustness problem by guaranteeing manifold solid output, making it a genuinely unusual rabbit hole.

entry.title: Manifold
entry.tldr: A C++ geometry library whose mesh Boolean operations are meant to always return a valid closed solid, with a web playground to try it.
entry.deeper_look:
Manifold is a library for building and combining triangle meshes that describe closed solid objects. You can make shapes with OpenSCAD-style constructors or from signed-distance functions, then union, subtract and intersect them, smooth and refine the result, and write it out. It has bindings for C, JS/TS via WASM, Python and several other languages.

The reason it exists is reliability. The README puts it this way: "Our primary goal is reliability: guaranteed manifold output without caveats or edge cases." It calls a robust mesh Boolean "an open problem for many years" and says this may be the first guaranteed-manifold one. Speed through parallelism, using TBB, is the second goal.

The idea underneath is what "manifold" means for a mesh: every edge joins exactly two faces and the surface encloses a volume, so the object could exist as a solid. Most mesh Boolean code can produce holes, stray edges or self-intersections on awkward input, and everything downstream then breaks. Manifold treats a valid solid as an invariant and tracks vertex properties and IDs so you can tell which input object each surface came from. The README links to a wiki for the algorithm details, which is the place to go deeper.

The project has opinions. It discourages STL export because STL loses topology, and points to 3MF or glTF with the EXT_mesh_manifold extension. Its user list includes OpenSCAD, Blender, Godot and BRL-CAD.
entry.install:
brew install manifold
This installs the C++ library and its dependencies (clipper2, tbb), with no executables. For quicker experiments, the README lists PyPI (manifold3d) and npm (manifold-3d) packages, or the ManifoldCAD web app, which needs no install.

try_this.what_happens: Inside a Python interpreter after importing manifold3d, prints the binding documentation so you can see what shapes and operations exist.
From a source checkout's Python examples, runs the samples and exports models. The README says to install trimesh and pytest first.
Fetches the source with submodules, the first step toward building it and running make test.

entry.whats_unique: Few mesh Boolean tools promise valid solid output, and this one says it is probably the first to do so. It also refuses to write STL files by design.
entry.caveats: Non-manifold input is rejected with an error and Merge only repairs slightly broken meshes, the WASM build is serial-only, and I could not confirm recent maintenance activity.
